extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to Lighthouse Writers Workshop programs (Book Project, Portfolio Year, Poetry Collective, Young Writers Program)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for applying to multiple Lighthouse Writers Workshop programs (Book Project, Portfolio Year, Poetry Collective, and Young Writers summer camps), including deadlines, admissions expectations, mentor fit, and program participation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are asked to 'please take your time with this application. Answer questions as fully and honestly as possible.' (stated for Book Project and Portfolio Year applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction to be thorough and honest when completing application questions. This is tied to programs that expect serious commitment (e.g., two-year Book Project).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline adherence / timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program has a firm application deadline: Book Project and Poetry Collective — apply by 11:59 PM MDT on June 22, 2026; Portfolio Year — apply by 11:59 PM MDT on July 1. Young Writers applications reviewed beginning January 2026 on a rolling basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to apply early. Portfolio Year cohorts may be grouped as applications roll in; applicants will be contacted about spots by mid-July (or within two weeks for Young Writers). Late or missing applications risk exclusion or placement on waitlist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program fit: seriousness and career goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Book Project: 'This is a two-year program for serious writers.' Portfolio Year: 'yearlong program for writers who want to break through in their writing careers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate commitment and readiness for intensive multi-month/ yearlong mentorship and cohort work; program placement depends on matching applicant goals to program intensity and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor/project alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentor bios and information about the projects they're seeking are provided, implying selection considers fit with mentor interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review mentor bios and project descriptions and tailor applications/materials to demonstrate fit with a mentor's stated project preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript cohesion (Poetry Collective)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poetry Collective is 'a manuscript-focused curriculum for poets... aimed at helping you produce a finished, high-quality book of poems that reads as a cohesive collection, not just a bundle of singular works.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions/works should demonstrate attention to sequence, thematic or formal coherence, and book-length craft rather than isolated poems; program curriculum focuses on producing a cohesive manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application review focus for Young Writers Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Lighthouse staff and faculty 'review each application, looking particularly at a student's expressed interest in writing and writing sample.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writing sample and the applicant's stated interest in writing are primary evaluative materials. Rolling review begins in January 2026; acceptance notifications within two weeks; waitlist if full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired applicant qualities for Young Writers Program
rubrics_metrics.description: The program seeks students who 'show a passion for writing, a creative spark, a desire to explore new topics, and openness to discovering new things.' Group dynamics and interpersonal qualities are also important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate enthusiasm, curiosity, and willingness to engage with peers. Expectation of respectful behavior toward instructors and peers and motivation to write. Diverse backgrounds and non-writing strengths are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination and accessibility regarding financial need
rubrics_metrics.description: The Young Writers Program states 'We do not discriminate based on the need for financial aid.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial need is not a barrier to admission consideration; applicants can request financial assistance via application sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and enrollment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment is required to secure a spot once an acceptance is received. For Young Writers Program the cost is $575.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After acceptance, applicants must register online, call with payment, or send a check to confirm spot. See the cancellation policy for refunds and cancellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assistance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Lighthouse offers a sliding scale for families who need financial aid; applicants should fill out the appropriate sections of the application form to request assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff will contact applicants about financial aid at the time of acceptance. The organization expresses a policy goal that all young people should have opportunity to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program schedule and participation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs include required dates/times: Book Project orientation (Aug 22) and intensives (fall and spring dates given); Poetry Collective intensives (specific monthly dates); Young Writers camp dates/hours (in-person, July middle/high school weeks, 9:30 AM–3:30 PM, not overnight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be available for listed orientation/intensive dates and in-person participation where applicable. Young Writers campers should bring lunch and may be invited to a public reading; campers may submit to an annual youth anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort formation and notification timing (Portfolio Year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Portfolio Year cohorts are formed as applications roll in; applicants 'will be contacted regarding spots no later than mid-July.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because cohorts form continuously, early applications may influence cohort composition and placement; applicants should indicate any scheduling constraints if relevant.
